title: Mediated effect of a source on a moving body

key_results.statement: The source stays at $\sigma_0$ for every $\lambda$: $\lvert\Psi(\lambda)\rangle=\lvert\sigma_0\rangle\otimes e^{-\mathrm iC^{(\sigma_0)}\lambda}\bigl(\lvert\beta\rangle\otimes\chi\bigr)$ and $V_{\{s\}}(\lambda)=\lvert\sigma_0\rangle\langle\sigma_0\rvert$; $b$ and $c$ are driven by the reduced contract $C^{(\sigma)}=C_b\otimes\mathbb 1_c+\sum_h\lvert h\rangle\langle h\rvert\otimes K_h+\mathbb 1_b\otimes(C_c+B_\sigma)$.
With $R_\sigma:=K_\beta+C_c+B_\sigma$ and $D_x:=K_x-K_\beta$, the reduced contract reads $C^{(\sigma)}=C_b\otimes\mathbb 1+\mathbb 1\otimes R_\sigma+\sum_x\lvert x\rangle\langle x\rvert\otimes D_x$.

$e^{-\mathrm iC^{(\sigma)}\lambda}=(\mathbb 1\otimes e^{-\mathrm iR_\sigma\lambda})\,\mathcal T\exp\bigl(-\mathrm i\int_0^\lambda C_I(s)\,\mathrm ds\bigr)$ with $C_I(s)=C_b\otimes\mathbb 1+\sum_x\lvert x\rangle\langle x\rvert\otimes D_x(s)$ and $D_x(s)=e^{\mathrm iR_\sigma s}D_xe^{-\mathrm iR_\sigma s}$; the first factor is a unitary on the companion of $b$, so the place weights $p_h(\lambda;\sigma)$ depend on the source only through the operator functions $D_x(s)$.

Sufficient condition for no influence: if $[\Delta,K_h+C_c+B_{\sigma'}]=0$ for every place $h$ of the moving body, with $\Delta=B_\sigma-B_{\sigma'}$, then $\delta p_h(\lambda)=0$ and $\delta\bar x(\lambda)=0$ for every $\lambda$; the condition and the influence are invariant under the placement convention (A5), the separate commutators with $K_h$ and $C_c$ are not.

For a chain of cells with the records on $c_1$ and the source on $c_{r+1}$: $\delta D_x(s)=D_x^{(\sigma)}(s)-D_x^{(\sigma')}(s)=\frac{s^{r+1}}{(r+1)!}\,Y_r^{(x)}+O(s^{r+2})$ with $Y_r^{(x)}=\mathrm i^{\,r+1}\bigl[\Delta,[J_r,[\cdots[J_1,D_x]\cdots]]\bigr]$ and $Y_r^{(\beta)}=0$; this nested commutator governs the influence: the lowest order at which $\delta p_h$ can be nonzero is $\lambda^{r+5}$, at $\beta$ and its neighbours, and $r=0$ is the case of one medium object.

For $h$ at graph distance $n$ from $\beta$: $\delta p_h=\frac{2\lambda^{2n+r+2}}{n!\,(n+r+2)!}\operatorname{Im}\Bigl[(t^n)^*_{h\beta}\sum_wt_w\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}\binom{r+1+j}{j}\langle Y_r^{(w_j)}\rangle\Bigr]+O(\lambda^{2n+r+3})$, summed over the walks $w=(w_0=\beta,\dots,w_n=h)$ with $t_w=\prod_jt_{w_{j+1}w_j}$; the coefficient vanishes for $n=1$ and whenever all products $t^*_{w'}t_w$ of shortest walks are real (real hopping, or a unique shortest path), and then $\delta p_h=O(\lambda^{2n+r+3})$.

$\delta p_\beta=-\lambda^{r+5}\sum_{h\sim\beta}\delta p_h^{(r+5)}+O(\lambda^{r+6})$, where $\delta p_h^{(r+5)}$ is the bracket coefficient of (18.7) and $h\sim\beta$ means $t_{h\beta}\neq0$, $h\neq\beta$; places at graph distance $\ge2$ contribute only from order $\lambda^{r+6}$.

For one medium object ($r=0$, $C_c=0$) and a neighbour $h$ of $\beta$: $\delta p_h=\lambda^5\Bigl[\frac{\lvert t_{h\beta}\rvert^2}{12}\operatorname{Im}\langle\Delta D_h^2\rangle+\frac16\sum_x\operatorname{Re}\tau_x\operatorname{Im}\bigl\langle\Delta(2D_x-D_h)\bigr\rangle\Bigr]+O(\lambda^6)$; also $\delta p_\beta=O(\lambda^5)$, and the coefficients of $p_h$ at orders $\lambda^2$ to $\lambda^4$ are source-independent.

With $s_{h\beta}:=\operatorname{Im}\langle\Delta\tilde D_h^2\rangle$, the source part of (6.11) for the pair $(h,\beta)$ with $B_{\beta_0}\to\Delta$, and $\epsilon_h=\langle K_h\rangle$: $\operatorname{Im}\langle\Delta D_h^2\rangle=s_{h\beta}+2(\epsilon_h-\epsilon_\beta)\operatorname{Im}\langle\Delta D_h\rangle$. The neighbour coefficient (18.9) is $\frac{\lvert t_{h\beta}\rvert^2}{12}s_{h\beta}$ plus a record-mean term and a triangle term, so it is not a function of $s_{h\beta}$.

$\delta\bar x=\lambda^{r+5}\sum_{h\sim\beta}\delta p_h^{(r+5)}\,(u_h-u_\beta)+O(\lambda^{r+6})$ with $\delta p_h^{(r+5)}$ the bracket coefficient of (18.7); for one medium object the lowest order is $\lambda^5$, with $\delta p_h^{(5)}$ from (18.9), and a common shift of all $u_h$ drops out.

The influence is independent of the cost difference $L(\sigma)-L(\sigma')=\langle\Delta\rangle$, since $\delta p_h$ and $\delta\bar x$ are unchanged under $\Delta\to\Delta+c\mathbb 1$; so the leading coefficient does not depend on the source only through its cost difference: $\Delta=c\mathbb 1$ has cost difference $c\neq0$ and exactly zero influence, while the example has $\langle\Delta\rangle=\sigma\langle\sigma_y\rangle=0$ and nonzero influence.

In the qubit example (places $h_1,\dots,h_n$, real $t$, $\sigma'=0$, $\Delta=\sigma\sigma_y$, start at $h_m$ with $2\le m\le n-1$): $\delta p_{h_{m\pm1}}=\frac{t^2\sigma^2}{45}\lambda^6+O(\lambda^8)$, $\delta p_{h_m}=-\frac{2t^2\sigma^2}{45}\lambda^6+O(\lambda^8)$ and $\delta p_{h_{m\pm k}}=O(\lambda^8)$ for $k\ge2$; the influence is exactly even in $\sigma$, unlike the background effect (6.14), (6.15), which is odd in $\sigma$.

In the example the position influence satisfies $\delta\bar x=O(\lambda^8)$ and is even in $\sigma$: its $\lambda^6$ coefficient vanishes and the odd orders vanish; its leading nonzero term is not determined.

open_issues: In the example, the leading coefficient of the position influence, at order λ⁸ or later, is not computed. It needs the λ⁸ terms of the 2-, 4- and 6-hop parts, and for m ≤ 3 or m ≥ n−2 also the chain ends. Even its non-vanishing is open.

The orders given by (18.6) and (18.7) are the lowest possible ones. Nonzero instances: (18.9) for generic records, and for (18.6) a square β, x, y, h with n = 2, whose coefficient is Im(conj(t_x) t_y) Im⟨(K_y − K_x) Δ⟩ / 6 with t_x = t_hx t_xβ and t_y = t_hy t_yβ. Exact vanishing conditions beyond these are not classified.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions: with [t] = [K] = [Δ] = [J] = [C] = [λ]⁻¹, the coefficient of (18.7) scales as [C]^(r+5) in both terms and that of (18.6) as [C]^(2n+r+2); restoring a record scale κ in (18.13) gives t²σ²κ²/45, of order [C]⁶.

Limits: for t → 0 the weights are p_β = 1 and p_h = 0 otherwise, exactly, and every coefficient is proportional to t²; if Δ is proportional to the identity or (18.4) holds, all Y_r^(x) vanish and so does the influence; for σ → 0 the result (18.13) is zero.

Special cases: for C_c = 0 the reduced contract is the contract of package 17 with records K_h + B_σ, and (17.10) depends on the records only through d_0(h, β) and differences of the means ε, which are invariant under this common shift, so the λ⁴ coefficient of δp_h vanishes as Step 6 states; the first term of (18.9) agrees with a direct Taylor expansion of ‖Φ‖², whose λ⁵ coefficient is (1/12) Im⟨Q_β D_h²⟩.
